items.currentRelevance: His 2025 exhibition The Need for Speed continued his exploration of movement, colour and contemporary visual culture. His 2026 group exhibition Bend Sinister, with Kottie Paloma, demonstrates an ongoing presence in the European gallery circuit.
items.excerpt: A collision of graffiti, pop culture and everyday absurdity, translated into paintings made without a safety net.
items.significance: Belgian artist Joachim Lambrechts emerged from the Antwerp graffiti scene, developing a visual language that carries the immediacy of street art into the studio. His paintings combine personal references, cartoon imagery and fragments of popular culture. His decision to work directly onto canvas, without preliminary sketches, gives the work an unpredictable energy that sits between controlled composition and spontaneous expression.
items.name: The Spontaneous Image
items.whyCollectorsCare: Lambrechts offers a recognisable visual identity without relying on a single recurring character or formula. His progression from street art into gallery exhibitions, alongside representation by Kristin Hjellegjerde Gallery, provides an established exhibition history. His inclusion in collections such as Colección SOLO and the Bunker Artspace adds institutional and private-collection context.

items.currentRelevance: His 2026 exhibition Threads at Louis Buhl & Co. and the museum presentation Lateral Hazard, with Stephanie H. Shih, demonstrate continued development across painting and digital culture. The relationship between his internet-based work and physical abstraction remains particularly relevant in an increasingly image-saturated art world.
items.excerpt: Hard-edged abstraction meets digital culture in paintings that turn familiar forms into unexpected optical experiences.
items.significance: Houston-based artist Paul Kremer occupies an interesting position between contemporary abstraction, graphic design and internet culture. His paintings use fluid acrylics and overlapping fields of colour to create forms that can suggest landscapes, architecture and natural phenomena. Alongside his studio practice, his Great Art in Ugly Rooms series became an internet phenomenon, digitally placing canonical artworks into deliberately unremarkable surroundings.
items.name: Colour in Formation
items.whyCollectorsCare: Kremer's practice offers two distinct but connected bodies of work: considered abstract paintings and digitally informed image-making. His paintings have been exhibited internationally, including with Berggruen Gallery and Library Street Collective, and his work is held in collections including the Birmingham Museum of Art. His auction history offers some secondary-market reference, although individual works and periods should be assessed carefully.

items.currentRelevance: The endless circulation of images, the collapse of visual hierarchies and the increasing influence of digital culture provide a compelling context for his work. Decamps transforms disposable internet material into considered physical objects, raising questions about authorship, originality and the value of images.
items.excerpt: Digital fragments, classical portraiture and surreal humour collide in meticulously constructed paintings.
items.significance: Belgian artist Yves Decamps approaches painting through the visual overload of contemporary life. Trained in photography, he collects fragments of found imagery from the internet and reconstructs them through digital manipulation and traditional painting. His compositions often combine seemingly unrelated subjects, creating portraits that are humorous, unsettling and deliberately ambiguous. His practice also draws on the visual heritage of Flemish painting and surrealism.
items.name: The Recycled Image
items.whyCollectorsCare: Decamps offers a distinctive approach to figurative painting at a time when the relationship between digital imagery and traditional artistic processes continues to evolve. His work is particularly interesting for collectors drawn to artists who interrogate contemporary image-making rather than simply reproduce it. His relatively limited public market visibility also means that provenance, gallery relationships and the development of his exhibition history deserve close attention.

items.currentRelevance: His ability to move between fine art, commercial collaborations and popular culture makes him an interesting case study in how contemporary artists build cultural relevance. The question for collectors is whether that visibility translates into lasting significance beyond the current cycle of attention.
items.excerpt: From Lagos skate culture to the international art scene, a confrontational visual language built for contemporary culture.
items.significance: British-Nigerian artist Olaolu Slawn emerged from Nigeria's skateboarding and streetwear communities before moving to London and developing his painting practice. His work combines graffiti, caricature, spray paint and deliberately irreverent references to popular culture. His 2023 commission to design the BRIT Awards statuette and stage established him as a significant figure beyond the conventional gallery circuit.
items.name: The New Pop Disruptor
items.whyCollectorsCare: Slawn's appeal extends beyond painting into fashion, music, celebrity and wider youth culture. His rapid rise has attracted substantial attention from collectors, although that visibility should not be confused with established long-term market stability. His output, edition structures and provenance need to be considered carefully, particularly given the volume of accessible merchandise and collaborations associated with his name.

items.currentRelevance: His 2026 solo exhibition Quantize Off at Ruttkowski;68 in Paris, alongside appearances at Art Basel Hong Kong, Frieze Seoul and The Armory Show, reinforces his international presence. His practice continues to bridge street culture and contemporary abstraction without being confined to either.
items.excerpt: Skateboarding, jazz and urban architecture distilled into rhythmic compositions of dots, lines and colour.
items.significance: Born in Seoul and now based in New York, Yoon Hyup developed a visual language informed by skateboarding, music and the changing geometry of urban environments. His paintings translate movement, rhythm and city lights into carefully balanced arrangements of dots and lines. Although often associated with street art, his work has a strong relationship with abstraction, particularly in its exploration of repetition, movement and spatial composition.
items.name: Rhythm of the City
items.whyCollectorsCare: Hyup has developed an international exhibition history spanning New York, Seoul, Tokyo, Hong Kong and London. His work is represented in collections including the Lotte Museum of Art and OAR Contemporary Art Museum, alongside corporate collections such as Dior and Tiffany & Co. His recognisable visual language offers collectors a coherent body of work with crossover appeal beyond the traditional contemporary art audience.

items.currentRelevance: Her 2026 inclusion in exhibitions at the Speed Art Museum and Fundación MEDIANOCHE0, alongside her 2026 presentation Bellosguardo, continues to expand her institutional and international visibility. Bull's work also speaks to a renewed interest in ambitious, materially rich abstraction.
items.excerpt: Expansive fields of colour and gestural abstraction that sit somewhere between landscape, memory and altered perception.
items.significance: New York and Los Angeles-based artist Lucy Bull has developed a distinctive approach to abstract painting, building complex compositions through successive layers of colour, gesture and translucent forms. Her large-scale works often evoke natural environments without depicting recognisable landscapes. The result is immersive painting that encourages prolonged looking, with shifting visual relationships that resist a fixed interpretation.
items.name: Abstract Immersion
items.whyCollectorsCare: Bull has moved beyond emerging-artist status into an increasingly established institutional and gallery context. Her work is represented by David Kordansky Gallery and appears in significant collections including LACMA, the Hirshhorn Museum, the Baltimore Museum of Art and the Albertina in Vienna. This institutional presence provides a stronger foundation for collecting than market attention alone. Her auction activity, however, still warrants careful consideration of individual works, scale and provenance.

items.currentRelevance: 2026 has brought a renewed run of exhibitions, including Recent Paintings at House of Chapters in France and 1-800-ASK-4ASS at Drey Gallery in Toronto. His 2026 book King of Los Angeles also continues his exploration of the relationship between visual art, storytelling and American culture.
items.excerpt: A distorted portrait of American life, where everyday scenes give way to absurdity, isolation and psychological unease.
items.significance: New York-based artist Jordan Sullivan works across painting, photography, writing and publishing. His paintings draw on the strange contradictions of contemporary American life, bringing together familiar environments, unsettling characters and moments of psychological disconnection. Beneath their often immediate, almost naive appearance lies a darker exploration of addiction, alienation, consumerism and the absurdity of everyday existence.
items.name: The American Unravelling
items.whyCollectorsCare: Sullivan's multidisciplinary practice gives his work a depth that extends beyond painting alone. His involvement in artist books, independent publishing and album artwork adds another dimension to his cultural position. His works have entered collections including HBC Global Art Collection and Memorial Sloan Kettering, although his secondary-market footprint remains comparatively limited. For collectors, this is a practice to understand through the work itself and its developing exhibition history rather than auction speculation.

items.currentRelevance: His 2026 exhibition Dire Straits at Carl Kostyál in Stockholm and Last Time I Met You the World Was a Different Place at Richard Heller Gallery in California demonstrate continued international gallery activity. His work remains an appealing proposition for collectors interested in contemporary figurative sculpture that combines technical skill with a strong individual personality.
items.excerpt: Surreal characters caught somewhere between childhood imagination, vulnerability and the awkwardness of being human.
items.significance: Swedish artist Joakim Ojanen creates an imagined world populated by strange, expressive figures. Working across sculpture, ceramics, painting and drawing, he gives his characters exaggerated features and distinctive personalities. Their awkward proportions and sometimes unsettling expressions explore familiar human emotions through an unfamiliar visual language. The result is playful, melancholic and occasionally grotesque.
items.name: Beautifully Uncomfortable
items.whyCollectorsCare: Ojanen's ability to translate a consistent visual language across different media makes his practice particularly interesting. His works are held in collections including Magasin III in Stockholm, Colección SOLO in Madrid and the Bunker Artspace in Florida. His sculpture has achieved a measurable auction history, with a reported auction record of US$25,000, although prices vary considerably by medium, scale and edition.
